title: MLLPA — Machine Learning-assisted Lipid Phase Analysis
summary: Transformation of a lipid-membrane research method into a documented and reusable Python module combining molecular dynamics, data analysis and machine learning.

sections.title: Scientific context
paragraphs: The project began at the University of Strasbourg as part of research into phase transitions in lipid membranes simulated through molecular dynamics.
items: Planning of methods, stages and scientific direction with a high degree of autonomy.
Study of lipid bilayers and their phase transitions, including the ripple phase.
Use of GROMACS, Linux, Bash and SLURM for simulations and scientific computing.

sections.title: Development of MLLPA
paragraphs: MLLPA was designed to make the analysis methods developed during the project available as a reusable Python tool.
items: Development of approximately 95% of the module’s code.
Creation of the entire website and documentation.
Structuring of data-processing workflows and membrane-phase analyses.
Public availability of the software, its website and documentation.

sections.title: Machine learning
paragraphs: The project incorporated several machine-learning approaches to analyse the states and transitions of membrane systems.
items: Development of methods based on scikit-learn.
Subsequent development of a three-dimensional convolutional neural network using TensorFlow.
The work related to the 3D CNN remains unpublished and continues occasionally through collaborations.

sections.title: Scientific results
paragraphs: The work resulted in several scientific publications as first author.
items: A machine learning study of the two states model for lipid bilayer phase transitions — Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics, 2020.
MLLPA: A Machine Learning-assisted Python module to study phase-specific events in lipid membranes — Journal of Computational Chemistry, 2021.
Ripple-like instability in the simulated gel phase of finite size phosphocholine bilayers — BBA Biomembranes, 2021.
